reasons: Errors are caught and ignored, so failures cannot be seen.
Repeated ambience changes leave small leftover volume nodes.
No tests are visible, and this is hard to test without a browser.

terms.meaning: the browser's built in system for generating and mixing sound
a generator that makes a tone at a set pitch
a volume control node in the audio chain

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File header and purpose
sections.what: Explains that all sounds are generated in the browser, so no audio files are needed and the sounds work offline.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the app light and reliable when hosted.

sections.name: SoundEngine, soundEngine (part 1)
sections.title: Setting up the audio context and click sound
sections.what: Creates the browser audio context the first time it is needed, resumes it if suspended, and plays a short falling click tone.
sections.why: Likely reason: browsers require an audio context, and clicks give quick feedback.
sections.watch_out: Browsers may block the first sound until the user has interacted with the page.

sections.name: SoundEngine, soundEngine: playComplete
sections.title: Completion chime
sections.what: Plays a two note chime for finishing something, with a short gap between the notes that fades out.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely reason: a pleasant reward sound for finished work.

sections.name: SoundEngine, soundEngine: playTimerBell
sections.title: Timer bell and starting ambience
sections.what: Plays a rising bell tone for timers. Also starts a background sound by first stopping any running one, then setting a volume and choosing the noise or drone builder.
sections.why: Likely reason: a timer needs an audible alert, and ambience should never stack.
sections.watch_out: Volume is multiplied by a fixed factor, so the slider value does not map directly to loudness.

sections.name: SoundEngine, soundEngine: stopAmbient
sections.title: Stopping ambience and reading its type
sections.what: Stops and disconnects every tracked sound node, clears the list, and returns the current ambience type when asked.
sections.why: Likely reason: stops background sound cleanly when the user leaves or changes it.
sections.watch_out: The volume control node is not removed here, so it stays connected after each stop.

sections.name: SoundEngine, soundEngine: if
sections.title: Building noise and drone ambience
sections.what: Builds a looping noise buffer shaped into rain, cafe or forest sound through a filter, or a two tone drone for lofi or space. Each new source is tracked so it can be stopped later.
sections.why: Likely reason: generating sound in code avoids shipping audio files.
sections.watch_out: The noise builder shapes sound with hand tuned numbers, which are hard to adjust without listening to them.

sections.name: playSound
sections.title: Mapping sound names to actions
sections.what: Takes a sound name and runs the matching action: complete and milestone play the chime, bell plays the timer bell, and anything else plays the click.
sections.why: Likely reason: one simple entry point keeps the screens from knowing about the sound engine.
sections.watch_out: An unknown name falls through to the click sound without any warning.

summary: Makes the app's sounds in the browser by generating tones and noise, with no sound files. It covers click sounds, a completion chime, a timer bell, and looping background ambience.
purpose: Play feedback sounds and looping background sounds such as rain, cafe, forest, lofi or space.
why: Likely reason: no audio files need to be shipped, and the sounds work offline. The file header says this directly.
how: 1. Creates one browser audio context on first use, and resumes it if it has been suspended. 2. Plays short tones for clicks, the completion chime, and the timer bell. 3. For ambience, builds looping noise or a drone, passes it through a filter and a volume control, and tracks those nodes. 4. Stops ambience by stopping and disconnecting the tracked nodes. 5. A shared function maps sound names to these actions.
inputs: A sound name such as complete, click, bell or milestone, and for ambience a type and a volume.
outputs: Audible sound in the browser. No files are written.
risks: Browsers block audio until the user interacts with the page, so the first sound can be silent. Each new ambience creates a gain node and the old one is never removed, a small leak over long sessions. Errors are swallowed, so failures are invisible.
debug: If no sound plays, click somewhere in the app first, then check the browser's sound permission and the app's sound setting. If ambience keeps playing after stop, check the list of tracked nodes. If sound gets quieter over time, check for leftover volume nodes.
